newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan seeks help from China to pursue kidnappers.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan seeks help from China to pursue kidnappers.

text.p: Taiwan on Tuesday sought help from rival China in the hunt for three suspects allegedly involved in the kidnapping and murder of the teenage daughter of a popular actress.

Police have issued warrents for the arrest of the three men, Chen Chin-hsing, Lin Chun-sheng and Kao Tien-min, over the kidnap and murder of 17-year-old Pai Hsien-yen, daughter of actress Pai Ping-ping.

"We have requested help from the mainland's Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Strait to pursue the suspects...who might have slipped into the mainland...," said Taiwan's semi-official Straits Exchange Foundation.

The foundation and its Chinese counterpart were set up in 1991 to represent their governments in talks after a thaw in relations in the 1980s. Taiwan and China split following a civil war in 1949 and Beijing still regards the island as a renegade province.
The foundation said it had sent pictures, finger print records and other relevant information detailing the crimes committed by the suspects to the mainland's association.
It called on China to repatriate the three if the suspects were arrested on the mainland.
Taiwanese were shocked by the discovery late last month of the body of 17-year-old Pai Hsien-yen. Her kidnappers had dumped her naked body in a river.
Around 50,000 people demonstrated on Sunday and staged an all-night vigil outside Taipei's Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall in protest at the island's worsening crime levels.
News media said public outrage had prompted Premier Lien Chan to consider a partial cabinet reshuffle in an effort to assuage growing resentment against the government.
A newspaper poll showed Lien's approval rating had sunk to a new low at a time of growing dissatisfaction with violent crime.
Only 24 percent of 762 people interviewed by the United Daily News on Monday said they were satisfied with his performance, down six percentage points from a similar poll a week ago.
